questions.question: In antenna array theory, a uniform linear array consists of isotropic radiators spaced by $d = \lambda / 2$ along the z-axis. To steer the main beam of the array factor to an angle of $\theta_0 = 60^\circ$ relative to the array axis, what progressive phase shift $\beta$ must be applied between adjacent elements?

An ideal continuous-conduction-mode (CCM) Buck converter operates with an input voltage $V_{in} = 24\text{ V}$, switching frequency $f_s = 100\text{ kHz}$, and output voltage $V_o = 12\text{ V}$. If the load power is $60\text{ W}$, what is the minimum inductance $L_{min}$ required to ensure the converter remains in CCM?

Consider a linear time-invariant system in state-space form with matrices $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$. What is the determinant of the controllability matrix $\mathcal{C} = [B \quad AB]$?

Two finite-length discrete sequences $x[n]$ of length $L_1 = 3$ and $h[n]$ of length $L_2 = 2$ are given. To compute the exact linear convolution of $x[n]$ and $h[n]$ using circular convolution via Discrete Fourier Transforms (DFT), what is the minimum DFT size $N$ required to avoid time-domain aliasing?

A uniform plane electromagnetic wave with frequency $f = 300\text{ MHz}$ propagates through a lossless, non-magnetic ($\mu_r = 1$) medium characterized by a relative permittivity of $\epsilon_r = 4$. What is the intrinsic impedance $\eta$ of this medium?
